Ligand 1 is my best molecule, and its numbering gives me two useful anchors: atom 1 is the amide carbonyl bonded to the cap at atom 17, and atom 11 is the azine carbon bearing the chlorine at atom 12 - both non-ring bonds. This episode takes the halogen. The C4 position is activity-insensitive across every compact group I have tried, so the choice there is really a drug-likeness choice, and chlorine is the heaviest and most lipophilic option I have used: this molecule sits at LogP 4.22, which is past where QED starts penalising. Fluorine is the obvious step down - 18 Da lighter and roughly half a log unit less lipophilic, while staying the same small, electron-withdrawing substituent that C4 appears to be indifferent to. If activity holds at 0.52, QED should improve by a couple of hundredths for free. A fluorine on the central ring cost me activity in run 1, but that was a different ring in a different electronic position, and C4 has tolerated everything so far.
